passages.title: Iron
passages.text: Iron is a mineral that is naturally present in many foods. Iron is an essential component of hemoglobin, an erythrocyte protein that transfers oxygen from the lungs to the tissues.

passages.title: Iron
passages.text: Acute intakes of more than 20 mg/kg iron from supplements or medicines can lead to gastric upset.

passages.title: Iron
passages.text: The labels for some of these products warn that iron supplements can reduce the absorption of levothyroxine tablets, and they advise against administering levothyroxine within 4 hours of iron supplements.

passages.title: Iron
passages.section: Groups at Risk of Iron Inadequacy
passages.text: During pregnancy, plasma volume and red cell mass expand due to dramatic increases in maternal red blood cell production. Iron deficiency during pregnancy increases the risk of maternal and infant mortality.

passages.title: Ashwagandha
passages.text: Common side effects are mild and include stomach upset, loose stools, nausea, and drowsiness. Since then, the use of ashwagandha has been linked to acute liver injury in other individuals.

passages.title: Ashwagandha
passages.text: Some experts advise against the use of ashwagandha by women who are pregnant. These findings suggest that ashwagandha might interact with thyroid hormone medications.
